scope: Quest event persistence and turn-in choice integrity in the current single-Map ownership domain. No new quest content, rates or reward formulas.
implemented: Accepted missions, objective updates, completion, abandonment and timer failure schedule a complete character snapshot at the end of the dispatched client/World/timer event, after reserved mail and child execution. GiveItem/DeleteItem/GiveSkill/DefendSkill and repeatable crafting also checkpoint their mutations without needing a stored mission row.

The snapshot contains quest counters/timers, consumed and granted inventory, currency, skills and child missions. Journal publication precedes clearing dirty flags; SQL failure retains the record for ordered replay. This removes the previous wait for periodic/logout saves for these quest changes.

Direct CS_QUESTEXEC_REQ and CS_QUESTDROP_REQ responses retain their original packet order but are buffered until the event checkpoint is durably published. Publication failure discards those responses, closes the session and retains dirty state. World/timer notifications are not response-buffered.

Persistent quest actions require a seeded item-ID allocator and the current main session. Replicas cannot execute quest actions or advance objectives. Existing DB-free tests, tournament save exclusions, main/DB-loaded snapshot gates and inventory prevalidation remain intact.

Missing, unknown, mismatched or foreign-class selected rewards are rejected before ingredients, currency or mission completion change. Normal items, magic prototypes and skills are covered. The original client's zero-selection sequence remains accepted when no class-applicable item/skill choice exists, including gold/EXP-only selected rows. Default/probability/random reward handling is preserved.

history_review.reason: Quest dirty state previously waited for periodic/logout capture while item mutations could flush earlier. An abrupt process exit could leave inventory and quest eligibility inconsistent. Selected reward validation previously allowed a missing/spoofed selection to consume a quest without its selectable reward. Regression cases reproduce both behaviors; neither repair changes publisher balance values.
history_review.entry_points: PlayerCheckQuest, DropQuest, ExecMission, OnQuestComplete, direct item/skill actions, timer expiry and CS_QUESTPOSEXEC. LoadQuestProgress does not schedule writes during admission. Client/World/timer/disconnect boundaries flush scheduled captures.

validation.platform: Linux .NET 10 SDK; source mounted read-only, no live SQL credentials in general smoke suites
validation.sql_scope: Synthetic quest graph through actual MapService client/World/timer dispatch and native SQL procedures in a separate disposable SQL instance. Each mutating child exits immediately without logout/SaveAll. A fresh process replays the event journal, reloads SQL state and performs the next step. Acceptance/starter items, hunt, turn-in/selected item/money/skill/next mission, repeat rejection, drop/reacceptance and timer failure pass.

remaining: RT_SOUL reward type 9 in 12 mission templates still fails closed pending a compatible award/packet/persistence contract. TT_WARREGION type 13 has 16 mail templates but no established event producer. Do not substitute EXP/soul-bar points or guess conquest rules.

SendPost character/mail child recovery is now implemented and SQL/process verified, including sibling/nested requests and stable uncapped issuance identity; see Gameforge/quest-mail-recovery.json. External world effects, cross-Map ownership and general pre-checkpoint incoming-event identity remain open. The audited 35 inherited SendPost templates have no TT_EXECQUEST children.

Checkpoints guarantee capture at the completed event boundary, not every intermediate instruction or a transaction across all character tables. World/timer packets are sent before that boundary; interruption during an event, ambiguous external effects and full server shutdown/restart still need acceptance testing.
Cross-Map owner fencing and routing remain incomplete. A local journal lease does not coordinate independently writing Map instances.

The actual MapWorker/client admission/logout/restart lifecycle, real-client quest journeys and pinned Gameforge content/balance compatibility remain unverified. Migration 041 and current source have not been deployed.
